question: How often do frozen models issue a wrong structural claim at the same target claim coverage, and does eight-step recurrence improve on the dedicated four-step model?
primary_statistic: Mean across five fits of shared conditional wrong-claim rate minus dedicated-four-step conditional wrong-claim rate, at policies calibrated to target coverage 0.75. Negative favors shared. Report achieved coverage and its paired difference jointly.
threshold_rule: For each model and fit, use the largest inclusive maximum-probability cutoff retaining at least ceil(target_coverage * calibration_size) calibration inputs. Include all ties. Labels are not used to select cutoffs.
phase_order: Read all checkpoint provenance; collect calibration predictions for all five fits; exclusively save all thresholds and artifact hashes in calibration-lock.json; only then generate or evaluate any final test input.
uncertainty: 2000 paired nonparametric bootstrap replicates resample the 20000 input indices with replacement, using the same resampled indices across both primary models and all five fits. Recompute each fit's conditional error ratio and then average differences. Report 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles, conditional on these fits and frozen calibration policies. Do not resample fits or claim coverage over future training runs.
secondary_outcomes: wrong claims divided by all inputs
individual fit results and between-fit range
interpretation: No automatic winner or equivalence claim. The primary interval measures input sampling uncertainty conditional on five fits and calibration. Matched target coverage does not imply matched held-out coverage. Secondary comparisons are descriptive and not multiplicity-adjusted.
scope: Frozen neural weights and trained depths; fresh coverage thresholds only. Same synthetic observation distribution as each checkpoint. Gaussian reference knows the synthetic prior and noise and is evaluated in CPU float64. This is a quality study, not a new verified-pipeline latency study or receipt proof.
stopping_rule: Complete the fixed five-fit, 20000-input test once. No outcome-dependent early stopping, threshold retuning, seed search, or model selection on final test labels. Preserve failed/partial runs separately. Any amended study requires a new protocol and fresh test seed.
